en: Contrary to the outdated belief that the Philippines has 7,107 islands, it actually comprises 7,641 islands.
Although many mistakenly think Mount Pulag is the highest peak, Mount Apo is actually the highest mountain in the Philippines.
Contrary to the common misconception that the Pampanga River is the longest, the Cagayan River is actually the longest river in the Philippines.
Despite the frequent mix-up with the western coast, the Philippine Sea is actually located on the eastern side of the archipelago.
Although often mistakenly called the smallest volcano in the world, Taal Volcano is actually just one of the smallest active volcanoes.
Contrary to the belief that the Philippine eagle only lives in Mindanao, it also naturally inhabits the islands of Samar, Leyte, and Luzon.
Despite the common misconception that Mayon Volcano is located in Camarines Sur, it actually sits entirely within the province of Albay.
Contrary to the belief that the Tubbataha Reefs are near Cebu, they are actually a UNESCO site located in the Sulu Sea off Palawan.
Although frequently mistaken for a Cebu attraction, the famous geological formation known as the Chocolate Hills is actually located in Bohol.
Contrary to the misconception that Baguio is the national capital, it is actually the regional capital of the Cordillera Administrative Region.
Contrary to the misconception that Quezon City is the national capital, the official capital of the Philippines is actually the city of Manila.
Contrary to the popular belief that Mount Apo is located entirely within Davao City, it actually spans the provinces of Davao del Sur and Cotabato.
